subject: Post-demo: throughput guardrails & streaming token budget for Zephyr pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@zephyr.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: throughput guardrails & streaming token budget for Zephyr pilot

Thanks again for the product walkthrough earlier — good session. Summary and immediate asks from our side so we can size the pilot cluster and validate SLOs: 

Quick recap
- Pilot goal: support Zephyr summarization and Q&A flows for beta users with predictable p95 latency and safe burst handling.
- Target SLOs discussed: p95 generation latency (non-streaming) <= 350ms, streaming tail (p99) <= 700ms for partial-token delivery.

Workload stats we captured during the call (please verify):
- Steady-state QPS: ~450 requests/sec
- Peak burst QPS: ~6,000 requests/sec (bursts last 8–15s, 1-minute smoothing shows ~2,200 QPS)
- Tokens per request: avg 420 tokens (distribution attached), median ~120, 99th ~2,400
- Streaming: ~8% of requests enable partial streaming (mostly long-doc summarization)
- Expected system concurrency at peak (requests in-flight): ~900 concurrent generations

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Alex/Priya: please send a 72-hour traffic trace (sampled) and a token-profile CSV (attached is the format we used). The trace helps us build a per-second token/time heatmap.
2) Redwood: we'll provide an initial throughput estimate and a recommended runtime config (batching, cache warm-up, streaming concurrency slots).
3) Confirm whether session affinity or per-user KV caching is required for the pilot (affects warm-cache hit rates).
4) Schedule a 30m follow-up on Friday (I proposed times via Calendly link).

Attachments: zephyr_token_profile.csv (attached), call recording (link in HubSpot notes).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Huang <alex.huang@zephyr.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@zephyr.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput guardrails & streaming token budget for Zephyr pilot

Thanks Marissa — attaching the sample trace as requested. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token distribution: median 120, 75th 480, mean ~420 (skewed by large-doc summarizations). 99th is ~2,400 as noted.
- Streaming: only the summarization flow streams partial tokens; interactive chat is server-side aggregation (no streaming). Streaming sessions average 18s; longest seen in our trace is ~95s.
- Concurrency: per-user concurrency is small (mostly 1–2), but multi-user peak across enterprise customers pushes system concurrency to ~900 during the 15s bursts.
- Affinity: for this pilot, session affinity would be nice-to-have but not required. We do expect better tail latency if KV cache stays warm per active session.

Attachments: zephyr_sample_trace.jsonl (72-hour sample, compressed).

On warm-cache: our engineering team can instrument warmup endpoints if Redwood prefers a short ramp period before allowing full traffic.

—Alex
Alex Huang | Head of Platform, Zephyr AI
alex.huang@zephyr.ai | (617) 555-3429

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Huang <alex.huang@zephyr.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput guardrails & streaming token budget for Zephyr pilot

Appreciate the trace, Alex — we skimmed the sample and generated a few quick notes. High-level sizing guidance (initial):

- Steady-state token throughput (approx): 420 tokens/request * 450 QPS = ~189k tokens/sec
- Peak token throughput (instant): 420 tokens/request * 6,000 QPS = ~2.52M tokens/sec (worst-case instant sustained over 10s)

Recommendations to meet the SLOs you asked for:
1) Batching & micro-batching: enable continuous batching with a max latency cap of 60ms to preserve p95 target. Prefer concurrency-aware batching (adaptive batch windows during bursts).
2) KV cache / warm-up: implement optional session warm-up endpoint. If affinity not guaranteed, configure a larger global KV rather than small per-session caches to improve hit rates during bursts.
3) Streaming slots: reserve ~120 streaming concurrency slots during peak to keep p99 streaming tail under 700ms (estimate based on token sizes you sent).
4) Instance class & quantization: recommend mixed instance pool (high-memory inference nodes + lower-latency streaming nodes). Use int8 quantization for CPU-offload of small requests; keep critical path on GPU for streaming.
5) Autoscaling policy: aggressive burst scale-up with fast graceful degradation path (fallback to shorter responses or smaller models) to avoid SLA violations.

Deliverables from Redwood by EOD tomorrow: 
- redwood_throughput_estimate.xlsx (high-level capacity table + cost buckets) — attached.
- A short config recommendation (batch sizes, streaming slots, KV sizes).

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the longest sustained streaming sessions you'll accept for the pilot? (you mentioned ~95s — is that rare or common?)
- Do you have any hard constraints on cold-start latency for new sessions (e.g., <200ms)?

I'll follow up with a slightly more detailed estimate after I parse the full 72-hour trace.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: throughput guardrails & streaming token budget for Zephyr pilot

Thanks — good clarifications. Quick actions and schedule: 

Action items
- Zephyr: please confirm whether long streaming sessions (~95s) are expected >1% of traffic. If yes, flag those sessions and we'll size for longer tails.
- Redwood: Karthik to produce a one-page pilot config + the workbook (attached) by EOD today.
- Procurement / legal: I'll send a short evaluation agreement for 90-day pilot via DocuSign (link included).

Scheduling
- I've added a 30-minute follow-up for Friday at 11:00 PT (Calendly link in thread). Please accept if the slot works.

Notes
- If affinity proves helpful, we can enable a short warm-up window during ramping to improve cache hit-rate without changing runtime code.
- We'll include a couple of fallback policies in the config: model fallbacks for peak width and response truncation policy to preserve latency SLOs.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the trace and the final sizing workbook.

Marissa
